# opencv

> An open-source résumé builder that stores nothing. A résumé lives entirely
> inside its own URL, so there is no account, no database and no API — which
> also means fetching a résumé link returns an empty page unless you know how
> to read it. This file explains how.

opencv is a static site. The editor runs in the browser and keeps documents in
localStorage; a résumé is shared by encoding the whole document into a link.

## Reading a share link

A share link looks like:

    https://brionmario.github.io/opencv/view#cv=z.q1bKS8xNVbJSKs5…

Everything after `#cv=` is the document. Because it is a URL *fragment*, the
browser never sends it to the server: every share link in existence arrives at
the host as the same request for `/view`, and the page is rendered client-side.
**Fetching a share URL can never return the résumé.** Decode it from the link
you already hold:

1. Split on `#cv=` and take the part after it.
2. Split that on the first `.`. The prefix is the codec: `z` = raw DEFLATE
   (`deflate-raw`, no zlib header), `u` = no compression.
3. The remainder is base64url (`-` and `_` for `+` and `/`, padding stripped).
   Decode it, then decompress if the codec was `z`.
4. The result is UTF-8 JSON: `{ "v": 1, "data": …, "theme": …, "layout": … }`.

`layout` is one of `professional`, `modern`, `classic`, `minimal`.

Older links carry `?data=<base64>` in the query string instead. Those hold the
bare document with no compression, theme or layout.

## The document format

`data` is opencv's internal shape, not JSON Resume. Top-level keys:
`personalInfo`, `experience`, `education`, `skills`, `projects`,
`certifications`, `awards`, `references`, `volunteering`, `strengths`,
`interests`, `publications`, `languages`, `socialLinks`, `customSections`,
`sectionOrder`. Entries carry `id` fields the editor uses to address them, and
text fields may contain inline HTML (`<strong>`, `<em>`, `<u>`, `<a>`).

It converts losslessly enough in both directions with
[JSON Resume](https://jsonresume.org/schema), which is what the tooling below
speaks. Prefer JSON Resume unless you specifically need opencv's own shape.

## Working with résumés programmatically

- [@brionmario/opencv-core](https://github.com/brionmario/opencv/tree/main/packages/core):
  the browser-free half — document model, section rules, the share codec
  (`encodeShare` / `decodeShare`), and JSON Resume conversion (`toJsonResume` /
  `fromJsonResume`). Runs under Node; `deflate-raw` and base64 are standard there.
- [@brionmario/opencv-mcp](https://github.com/brionmario/opencv/tree/main/packages/mcp):
  an MCP server. Tools: `list_templates`, `get_sample_resume`, `create_resume`,
  `read_resume`, `update_resume`. Takes and returns JSON Resume, and mints share
  links pointing at this site (or another, via `OPENCV_BASE_URL`).

## Pages

- [/](https://brionmario.github.io/opencv/): dashboard — the résumés held in this browser.
- [/templates](https://brionmario.github.io/opencv/templates): the four templates, previewed.
- [/editor](https://brionmario.github.io/opencv/editor): the editor. Operates on the open document; takes no résumé in the URL.
- [/view](https://brionmario.github.io/opencv/view): renders a shared résumé read-only. Needs the `#cv=` fragment to show anything.

## Notes

- A link *is* the document. It cannot be revoked, it works for anyone who holds
  it, and editing produces a new link rather than changing the old one.
- Links run to a few KB and break if truncated.
- [Source](https://github.com/brionmario/opencv) · MIT.
